canal_p13_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_001.text: Rain had been falling on the ridge for half a day when the landing guild met on the thirtieth morning. At the canal, the water still lay below its ordinary caution mark. One trustee called the emergency request premature. Luo placed the down-fork route drawing beside the dated upper rain note. Waiting for local water to rise before booking a qualified crew would leave the same ordinary travel time with less room around it. She asked for preparation and response hours whose actual use could be checked afterward.

canal_p13_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_002.text: The guild chair wanted the people below the fork represented in the request. The garden correspondent had sent the accepted low-flow report, the tenant's slower escape interval and the reed shelter's completed relocation. Their current exposure was visible without pretending a flood had already harmed them. Han spoke for his private loading plot, where he would move his goods at his own cost. The chair asked him whether he still claimed title over the common hollow. He said the corrected register gave him none.

canal_p13_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_003.text: The separately authorized allocation passed after the guild recorded its weather evidence and specific tasks. Thirty-six copper went to the emergency receiver: twenty-four for eight worker-day equivalents at three copper, eight for material and four for two charged stones. The original repair account stayed distinct. The emergency order permitted preparation and actual response within those totals, with unused hours and material reported. The trustees named their receiving authority before money left the guild box. Yue watched the purse cross the table, relieved that tomorrow's help now had a source.

canal_p13_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_004.text: The paid response schedule assigned two day equivalents each to Yue, Bao and Jiang, and one each to the two trained road workers. Each equivalent meant the posted accepted hours, including necessary booked travel and standby intervals within the quoted appointments. The road crew's ordinary checked line gear came with its hire. Luo's regular keeper observations remained in operations. Eight equivalents could not become eight people on every night shift. The receiver wrote their actual intervals while Yue compared them with the slower ground departure below the fork.

canal_p13_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_005.text: Jiang accepted the new appointment through the workshop receiver before boarding the scheduled local boat. Her earlier three ordinary equivalents were already complete and paid. These two emergency equivalents would cover fresh inspection, scheduled readiness and any accepted live control work within the finite hours. Bao sent the current apparatus condition and actual trial-path gauge record. Yue did not replace its remaining count with the conservative lower bound. The crew would start from the charge that really remained in the case their chosen trial had left.

canal_p13_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_006.text: The material order used six copper for brace and guide pieces, two for weather covers and tie stock. The two additional stones arrived with separate receiving marks and forty measured charge units each, bought for four copper in total. Their eighty units joined the existing supply record without recharging it from the storm. Bao placed the purchased timber above ordinary splash level. Han shifted his own surplus sale goods higher in the private store. Both acts prepared wood for water; only one belonged to the public emergency account.

canal_p13_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_007.text: The guild's dissenting trustee asked whether the paid crew should work even if the rain stopped. The receiver showed the actual preparation tasks and limited standby intervals already offered. Those hours could earn payment while reducing current exposure, but no unused live-work interval would be certified merely because it had been budgeted. Yue liked hearing that answer until she saw her own two new equivalents. She wanted every hour to become impressive. The sheet would pay useful work, not a performance large enough to justify a decision already made.

canal_p13_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_008.text: A runner from the upper orchard landing arrived during the meeting with a fresh reading. The ridge rain had continued overnight, and a roadside ditch was carrying water into a shallow quarry hollow above the canal branch. Its ordinary overflow lip remained intact when he left. The note named his view and its time. Luo asked for another report through the same real route rather than treating an intact lip at dawn as a forecast for night. Bao marked the quarry hollow outside the old canal survey.

canal_p13_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_009.text: Han knew the quarry because his store once bought stone there. He said the hollow had drained slowly toward the upper branch after each ordinary shower. The current owner had raised a low stock bank to keep carts dry. Han had not seen it since spring. Yue wanted that memory to explain the new note immediately. Bao asked for the present bank height and outlet condition before choosing an explanation. A remembered quarry could point them toward a real question without answering what the rain was doing there today.

canal_p13_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_010.text: The quarry receiver answered by ordinary boat message that its owner would allow the public drainage officer to inspect the accessible outlet that afternoon. The canal crew would not leave its own exposed works to dig at an upstream private bank. Luo sent the actual request to the officer and paid the ordinary message from operations. Yue copied the contact and time. There were limits to what their own commission could reach, even when a new piece of ground seemed capable of changing everybody's night.

canal_p13_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_011.text: At the lock, the keeper replacement found the ordinary caution mark clear and the repaired cap moving without a catch. Luo entered that reading beside the upper warning. The two facts disagreed only if somebody expected local water to rise at the same instant as distant rain. Yue wrote their times in separate columns. A cargo pilot wanted to leave while the ordinary route remained open. Luo checked his current load and passage interval, then let him use the service still actually available. The warning did not make every present trip a reckless one.

canal_p13_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_012.text: Tian arrived with weather covers cut from the emergency order's purchased cloth. Her private sewing quote came within the two-copper cover-and-tie material line; no extra unpaid repair shift was assumed. She had finished her market order first. Yue liked seeing her receive a material task as a working seamstress rather than a household successor conveniently available on the bank. Tian said the covers would fit if Bao kept his fittings inside the dimensions he had sent. Bao solemnly promised not to enlarge the rain.

canal_p13_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_013.text: The road workers walked the actual higher landing retreat with the grandmother and her son during their accepted preparation interval. They carried ordinary lamps and checked their own line gear, using it only where the work plan required. The grandmother showed them the resting bench and her light sack. One worker asked what phrase she would hear. She repeated the practiced full departure instruction. Her son watched without improving it. The response now had people who knew the slower walk because they had actually walked beside her.

canal_p13_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_014.text: Bao checked the guide braces against the low-flow record and current ground before adding the emergency pieces. The new stock strengthened specific accessible supports within their checked working conditions; it did not turn the whole hollow into a wall against any flood. He kept the outer channel's soft clay under observation and left the ordinary ground route clear. Yue helped carry light tie stock during her booked preparation hours. The new job had a higher wage, but her arms still lifted the same small ordinary weight.

canal_p13_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_015.text: The garden owner returned from market with the actual low-flow report already read. She was less surprised by the crew than the rumors had prepared her to be. She wanted to know whether her ordinary private outlet could remain open during precautionary closure of the canal feeder. Bao showed its separate path and checked condition. If higher water began backing there, the owner or nearer observer would report the actual mark and the crew would stop exposed work. The house would use its ground departure rather than waiting for a small board to solve a large head.

canal_p13_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_016.text: The gardener harvested the low edge of his beans while the ordinary weather still allowed it. He wanted the response crew to help carry the crop. Their paid intervals covered guide preparation and people, not his private harvest. Han offered his ordinary private cart at its actual small fare. The gardener grumbled, then hired it after comparing what he could carry alone. Yue helped tie one loose basket during a break after being asked, but made no promise to turn the whole crew toward a field because the beans felt urgent.

canal_p13_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_017.text: By afternoon, Jiang arrived with the new appointment copy and a bundle of sour plums that belonged to her, not the supply order. She inspected the actual case seals and read its surviving trial gauge before connecting the added stones. The original six held the precise chosen-path remainder; the new pair added eighty. The starting emergency lower bound was two hundred seventy-eight, while the actual higher count stayed on the signed gauge record. Yue handed over the copied trial sequence. Their new response began from what had really happened, including its first stop.

canal_p13_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_018.text: Jiang checked the powered selector and actuator unloaded, drawing two supply units for the accepted dry comparison. She then tested the ordinary manual equivalent with the supply isolated. The actual remainder fell by those two, with a conservative floor of two hundred seventy-six. The apparatus retained its bounded operating rating and current control path. Yue could prepare one small command if later conditions permitted, but her stage had not widened because the guild bought more charge. Jiang accepted the clean dry response and covered the contacts against the actual coming weather.

canal_p13_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_019.text: The sky above the canal remained pale through the afternoon, making the distant rain note look less convincing to people watching only their own roofs. A boy announced that the guild had paid three copper to make everyone afraid of clouds. Tian told him it had paid for work and asked whether he wanted to see the new cover fit. He held its clean edge outside the marked fitting space while she checked the shape. A rumor lost some energy when its speaker found an ordinary object more interesting.

canal_p13_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_020.text: The upstream drainage officer's report arrived before dusk. The quarry's raised stock bank had narrowed its ordinary outlet, and collected water was approaching the reported overflow lip. The officer had ordered a current restricted clearing by the quarry's responsible crew and notified the public road receiver. He did not guarantee that the hollow would drain before more rain. Bao added the source and observed hour to the canal plan. Their own response could prepare for a possible quicker rise without claiming the quarry had already caused a flood.

canal_p13_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_021.text: Han wanted to send two store workers uphill with shovels. The officer's assigned crew had the actual current outlet instructions; uncoordinated digging might release held water at a worse time. Luo asked Han to offer help through that receiver if his workers agreed and were qualified. Han accepted after reading the report twice. He was frightened for his private goods and wanted a visible act. The receiver gave him a real contact rather than the permission to feel useful by arriving at somebody else's held water.

canal_p13_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_022.text: Yue wrote to the grandmother that the actual departure call would come through the checked nearer route if conditions required. She did not tell her to fear a quarry she had never seen. The message named the preparations already complete and the existing higher bench. The son brought it indoors and read it without adding his own warning. His mother sent back that the sack was ready and the tea pot would stay behind. Yue put that small practical answer in the response cover beside the much larger upstream figures.

canal_p13_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_023.text: The road crew inspected the lower public strip after the gardener's cart passed. A wheel had pressed its outer edge despite the crossing's foot-only limit. The cart driver admitted he had mistaken the narrow board for the older cart route. Bao closed that outer point and directed people along the already checked inner strip while he assessed the actual disturbance. Han's cart service report would include the driver's wrong route. A private fare did not purchase permission to ignore a public crossing's stated load.

canal_p13_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_024.text: The pressed edge had shed loose surface gravel but left the underlying inner footing sound. Bao repaired the reachable shoulder using the emergency brace stock already assigned to that location and checked the foot-only board anew. The driver helped move his empty cart back by the actual level route. He paid his own private handling loss; no household was blamed for failing to guide him. Yue felt angry that an avoidable mistake had consumed time before rain. The repair still had to answer the ground rather than reward her anger.

canal_p13_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_025.text: Luo ordered the foot-only sign made larger before dusk and asked the path receiver to explain the alternate cart route at both ends. Tian used the remaining marked cover cloth offcut for a weather-resistant arrow within the purchased material, with the receiver checking its direction. The driver read it aloud and confirmed where his next wheels would go. The current crossing was open again for its intended feet and baskets. It would close if actual higher-water marks or footing left the checked limits, whatever a impatient traveler preferred.

canal_p13_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_026.text: The evening reading showed the canal beginning a slow local rise below its caution mark. Distant rain had finally become present water, but not yet the sharp change the quarry note made possible. Luo moved the planned late cargo interval earlier while the checked conditions remained. The pilot accepted the change after receiving the actual head and expected duration. Yue watched his boat leave in ordinary light. The bank still had choices before its ground route became an emergency, and using them felt less dramatic than waiting to need courage.

canal_p13_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_027.text: Three preparation tasks remained before the last ordinary passage. Jiang wanted the covered command path and manual fallback checked from the operating position; Luo wanted the upstream warning receivers compared against their actual current report times; the road crew wanted the lower escape route's lamps and handover points tested in fading light. All belonged to accepted emergency intervals already funded. Yue could work beside the small control, beside the changing information or beside the people who might have to leave the house after dark.

canal_p13_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_028.text: The current local mark was still below caution. Yue felt the pressure to finish everything before darkness, even though choosing one task would leave the others in capable hands. Bao had his remaining preparation interval and Jiang her booked readiness hours. Luo's keeper schedule continued through the night. The road workers would report actual route checks rather than stand forever merely because the weather was unsettled. The response had a finite shape, and tonight's choice would determine which part Yue understood most closely when the first urgent call arrived.

canal_p13_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_029.text: Yue could check the small selector with Jiang, compare the real weather messages with Luo or walk the ground departure with the road crew. The new appointment and supply had been accepted; the original accounts and actual trial remainder remained visible. Outside, the sky above the canal was still brighter than the ridge reports suggested. She would have to learn a night whose danger came through ordinary distant observations before it could be seen from the window where she wanted to sleep.

choices.text: Check the covered control path with Jiang.
Compare actual weather messages with Luo.
Walk the lit ground route with the road crew.

canal_p13_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_030.text: Jiang set the covered selector on its accepted dry support while Yue stood at the marked operating position. The cloth kept rain off the contacts, but one tied corner hung near the manual release. Yue noticed it before Jiang asked for the fallback demonstration. They shifted the tie to its proper fixed point and checked the handle's full unloaded travel. The cover had fitted Bao's dimensions. Its fastening still needed the current operator's hands to show where an ordinary loose edge could interfere.

canal_p13_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_031.text: Yue traced the command on the unpowered comparison tile without sending a live sequence. Her arm pairs stayed within their recovered baseline after the ordinary field days. Jiang watched the small gesture and asked what Yue wanted from the next threshold. Yue said she wanted to be useful sooner. Jiang asked whether that meant stronger, faster or less dependent on someone asking her to wait. The question annoyed Yue because she could not decide which answer she hoped would sound best.

canal_p13_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_032.text: She finally said she wanted a mistake to cost less when she made it. Jiang took a sour plum from the bundle and considered that answer. Stronger work could make a mistake larger if its operator trusted confidence more than current conditions. Yue knew the principle and resented hearing it when she wanted comfort. Jiang offered the plum instead of another sentence. They ate in silence while the dry selector waited, ordinary enough to keep working after both of them admitted they were tired.

canal_p13_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_033.text: Jiang had once repeated a beautiful little command until her fingers lost their ordinary fine grip. She described the failure without making it a complete moral tale. Rest brought the grip back; the delayed repair disappointed a receiver who had booked his cargo. Her teacher made her pay the real extra carriage from later wages. Yue asked whether she hated the teacher. 'That week,' Jiang said. 'The receiver still deserved the fare.' Yue turned the cold tile over and saw her own wish for a harmless error become harder to name.

canal_p13_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_034.text: The manual fallback needed two ordinary movements from the operator, with the control isolated before the geared handle took the small release. Yue rehearsed the order on the unloaded mechanism under Jiang's current appointment. The hand path worked from the marked dry position without leaning into the moving guard. She asked whether she should practice faster. Jiang asked for a clear second repetition at ordinary pace. Speed would be useful only after the actual sequence survived a calm hand twice.

canal_p13_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_035.text: A small copper contact cap had loosened during the cover adjustment. Jiang tightened its proper fixing with the power isolated and checked the mechanical guard before accepting the path again. Yue copied the exact change instead of writing that the whole selector had failed. The two-unit powered comparison already completed its current dry response; this reachable fixing correction required no new live draw. Jiang kept the supply isolated afterward. The case could remain ready without using charge to reassure an apprentice every time a screw moved.

canal_p13_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_036.text: The road worker came to ask where his ordinary stopping call would meet the operator's hearing. Jiang stood at the selector while he called from the current clear position, then turned her body enough to keep the release in view. Yue heard how rain on the cover might drown the first syllable later. They chose a nearer relay position already inside the checked apron and repeated the full call. The response used a real voice with a real clear path, rather than assuming the cover only solved problems.

canal_p13_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_037.text: Jiang marked the current head condition on the selector's operating sheet. If the little pocket or actuator left its accepted rating, there would be no powered command merely because water now needed somewhere to go. The crew would close work and use ground retreat before the larger external flow made the position unsafe. Yue asked how she would know whether that moment came. Jiang pointed to the independent observer and fixed mark, then asked her to name the actual ordinary route she would take after hearing it.

canal_p13_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_038.text: Yue walked that route from the selector while the supply stayed isolated. One tie bundle sat beside the last dry turn, left by a worker who expected to return in a minute. She moved it to the assigned stock spot after its receiver agreed. Jiang followed at a slower pace, noticing the same corner from her own wider stance. Their feet gave the drawing a current width. Yue came back calmer, having done something more useful than asking her arm routes whether courage felt different from impatience.

canal_p13_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_039.text: At the counter, Jiang submitted the corrected cover tie, reachable contact fixing and actual hearing position. Yue added the walked retreat and kept the apparatus gauge at its true post-inspection count. No live command had been spent during this preparation branch. Her routes remained recovered for a later permitted task. She felt less prepared to do everything and more prepared to stop doing the wrong thing. Jiang accepted the handover, then went to her booked rest place before another discussion could eat its whole interval.

canal_p13_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_040.text: Luo spread the upper weather notes beside the actual keeper log. Yue sorted them by observed time before delivery time. The quarry lip intact at dawn came before the officer's report that water approached it in the afternoon. A pilot had brought the later note faster, making it arrive first at the lower landing. The two accounts had seemed to contradict one another when read by arrival order. Their actual times formed a changing situation, less reassuring but much easier to understand.

canal_p13_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_041.text: One note lacked an observed hour, giving only the departure date. Luo asked its receiver for the missing time through the ordinary message route. Yue wanted to place it between the other two by its damp wrapper. Luo laughed and said boats could wet paper long after the writer left home. They marked the hour unknown until the receiver answered. The little gap did not invalidate the dated reports already available. It did stop them from making a tidy sequence out of a paper that had not supplied its place.

canal_p13_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_042.text: The upper drainage officer's second note described the quarry's restricted clearing still underway. Its crew had found loose stock stone near the outlet lip and stopped for support assessment before removing the piece. Luo entered the actual pause. Han wanted the canal to order them to continue. Their officer had current ground the canal did not possess. Yue asked Han to put his concern through the same receiver instead. He wrote that delayed overflow could reach private cargo and public houses alike, a useful warning without a false instruction.

canal_p13_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_043.text: At the toll counter, a traveler claimed he heard the quarry bank had already burst. His source was another passenger who had heard the officer mention held water. Luo asked for the exact witness and time. He had neither. Yue recorded the rumor as unverified in the message margin and kept it off the current observed-warning board. The traveler looked offended that his dramatic news became a small uncertain note. Luo told him he could bring an actual witness later. For now, people needed to know which road truly remained open.

canal_p13_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_044.text: The local caution mark stayed clear through their first comparison. Yue read it herself from the keeper's stable viewing point, then checked the reading with the ordinary operator. The upper warnings justified readiness before a local rise. They did not yet justify claiming the canal had reached a level it had not. Luo put both states on the board in plain words. Han said people would think she could not decide. She said a decision to prepare could stand beside a decision to let the current safe boat pass.

canal_p13_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_045.text: The missing observed hour returned by message before dusk. That note belonged to a late morning view of the intact quarry lip, before the officer's afternoon warning. Yue placed it properly without erasing its initially unknown state from the received record. The receiver had answered a real question. Luo sent acknowledgment and asked the next report to carry both hour and departure route. Accuracy became easier when ordinary messages named what a distant reader actually needed, rather than assuming everyone shared the same sight of the bank.

canal_p13_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_046.text: The clerk had copied the quarry's current owner as its former leaseholder on the contact sheet. Han recognized the old name and offered the current business receiver from a purchase letter he chose to share. Luo checked it against the officer's current reply before changing the official contact. Yue thought about Pei's scratched household line. Names could remain in a system long after their associated authority moved elsewhere. This correction concerned today's warning recipient, and an accurate current contact mattered more than the pleasure of finding another old error.

canal_p13_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_047.text: Tian read the plain warning board while waiting for cover payment. She understood the observed ridge rain, current quarry concern and local mark without needing the detailed officer report. She said the board made the danger sound possible rather than certain. Luo said that was its actual state. Tian asked whether they would warn the tenant now or wait until certainty. The current preparation message had already gone. A later departure call would come from the agreed actual trigger, with enough time for the slower route they had walked.

canal_p13_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_048.text: Yue carried the current plain summary to the garden landing through the actual evening pilot. The tenant's nearer receiver accepted it and read back the distinction between readiness and departure. The grandmother would keep her sack prepared tonight without moving merely because a passenger told a frightened story. Luo's next timed report would use the same route if it remained open, with the road crew's near call available during the accepted response interval. The message now had a person who could repeat what it meant from the house side.

canal_p13_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_049.text: At the counter, Yue submitted the ordered observation times, corrected current receiver and separate uncertain rumor. The local rise was now visible but below caution, matching the final keeper reading. Luo read the complete sequence and arranged the next actual update time. Their information branch had consumed ordinary message time and no apparatus charge. Yue watched a moth circle the lamp and thought how little a useful warning resembled prophecy. It needed dates, contacts, a voice and somebody willing to wait without calling uncertainty an answer.

canal_p13_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_050.text: The road workers took Yue below the fork before the last ordinary passage, carrying checked lanterns from their own hired gear. The grandmother met them at the gate with the light sack ready but no current departure call. Her son wanted to light every lamp at once. The nearer worker kept one protected lantern at the yard corner and another at the bench, leaving the route's turns visible without shining into the observers' eyes. Yue walked from the actual doorway to see what their lights made easier and what they hid.

canal_p13_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_051.text: The first lamp cast a bright reflection on the wet stone beside the step. Beyond it, the inner route looked darker by contrast. The worker moved the lamp to its sheltered side and used its owned shield to keep the direct flame out of arriving eyes. Yue walked the turn again. The path's rise showed clearly without inviting her foot toward the brighter soft edge. The grandmother said she could see where to put a boot now. An expensive flame would not have helped if its light pointed to the wrong place.

canal_p13_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_052.text: The son brought a household candle and wanted to set it on the foot-only board. The road worker asked him to keep the private candle indoors because wax near the working crossing could confuse its boundary and blow out in the open wind. He accepted after seeing the actual lamp positions. His urge to help had become easier to redirect since the shutter repair. Yue thanked him for showing what a person might naturally add in a hurry. They could explain that before warning, when there was still room for an ordinary answer.

canal_p13_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_053.text: At the bench, the grandmother asked whether somebody would wait for her if the lamp went out. The response assigned a named road worker during its actual paid ground interval. Outside that interval, the regular nearer warning receiver would give the route call and ask for current help through the landing. The plan did not promise a permanent guard. She accepted the distinction after hearing the real available times. Yue disliked its finite shape, then remembered that an unlimited sentence would leave her waiting for a person nobody had hired.

canal_p13_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_054.text: They checked the lamps' ordinary oil level against their accepted readiness period. The crew's quote included its checked lantern gear and fuel for the booked response, with no second charge to the cover-material line. One lamp's wick needed trimming before its flame held cleanly. The worker did that in a stable place away from the purchased cloth and dried ties. Yue watched the smoke settle. A reliable lamp required the little task its owner actually knew, not a spirit bright enough to compensate for an ignored wick.

canal_p13_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_055.text: The reed gatherer passed on his way to the higher shed and saw the new lights. He asked whether tonight was the departure warning. The road worker repeated the readiness state in full words and showed him the plain board. The gatherer continued to his already relocated bed. Yue saw how a lantern placed for safety could become rumor without its own explanation. They added a short readiness label at the landing, where curious walkers could read it without entering the lit work route.

canal_p13_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_056.text: A boy came running after a dog that had taken his old bread heel. The dog crossed the inner path and vanished into reeds outside the soft hollow. Yue stopped the boy before he followed. The road worker called the animal from stable ground with the boy's familiar whistle while the grandmother offered a fresh crust at the safe corner. The dog returned reluctantly. The boy retrieved his heel, then admitted it was no longer food he wanted. They kept him on the ordinary path and left the dog with its actual owner.

canal_p13_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_057.text: The grandmother laughed after the boy left, saying every emergency plan needed a dog who had not read it. The road worker said he preferred finding the problem while the feeder was quiet. Yue checked the route's low rail where the boy had tried to pass. Its ordinary closure remained sound. They made no new fence from unpurchased material, but the nearer receiver would keep children at the public landing during any live response. The evening's small interruption gave that instruction a real example.

canal_p13_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_058.text: Before returning, Yue walked the grandmother's route once more with the light sack carried at the woman's actual pace. The protected lamps showed the stable inner line. They paused at the bench and continued to the higher landing without crossing the soft depression. The road workers noted the elapsed time within their current response interval. Her son did not ask why she walked slowly. He asked whether the sack's strap rubbed her hand. She gave it to him for a small household padding repair after the rehearsal.

canal_p13_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_059.text: At the counter, the road crew submitted the checked lamp positions, actual oil interval and repeated slower walk. Yue brought the readiness label and the nearer receiver's child-watching instruction. The dog had gone home; the grandmother had kept her sack indoors until a real departure call. No apparatus charge was used. Tomorrow's ground response would begin from a route people could actually see, and from a woman who had walked it with the people hired to stand beside her.

canal_p13_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_060.text: The three evening reports reached the emergency receiver before the last ordinary boat. The selector's cover and call positions were clear, the weather notes carried their proper observation times, and the lower route's protected lamps had passed the actual slower walk. Yue heard the tasks she had not followed from their own workers. The post-inspection apparatus count remained its true chosen-path remainder plus eighty minus two. The little case did not need to be used tonight merely because the crew could now describe how it would work.

canal_p13_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_061.text: Luo closed ordinary late cargo before the local mark reached caution, using the posted precautionary interval agreed with the landing receivers. A pilot who had hoped for one more trip complained about the lost fare. She recorded his actual canceled booking for the later loss review rather than offering relief money already assigned to response. He took his empty boat to the higher mooring. Han watched and moved his own cart under cover. Their private inconvenience had begun before the first flooded yard.

canal_p13_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_062.text: The night keeper took the current local reading and confirmed the new response contacts. Jiang went to her booked rest after finishing the accepted inspection. The two road workers split their readiness intervals so both were not promised awake through every hour. Bao covered the field tools and told Yue to eat before checking her next task time. The funded crew had to remain useful tomorrow. Tiredness would not disappear because the warning came from somewhere its members could not see.

canal_p13_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_063.text: On the thirty-first morning, the sky finally darkened above the canal. Fine rain made little rings on the ordinary water. The local reading approached caution slowly. The upper drainage officer sent word that the quarry outlet support was restored and restricted clearing had begun, with a fresh measured view still due later. Luo entered that partial improvement without calling the held hollow empty. Yue could imagine the report as reassurance if she wanted to sleep better. She kept its incomplete receiving state visible instead.

canal_p13_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_064.text: Bao walked the guide braces during his accepted emergency preparation interval. One tie had stretched after the cover became wet. He reset it from the dry side and checked the support without loading the small board beyond its rating. The field shoulder remained in place under ordinary rain runoff. The road crew checked the inner departure strip after the same shower. These current observations mattered more than yesterday's successful low feed. Yue helped carry the light stock and watched mud begin coloring a channel that had looked empty three days ago.

canal_p13_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_065.text: The garden owner brought her planned market journey forward, choosing to remain near the house before the current warning changed. She still had private business to finish and asked her son to carry its seed parcel to the actual receiver. He could go because the tenant's ground support had a named paid worker during the critical interval. The grandmother wanted him to take the finished shutter receipt too. He laughed at finding another paper inside a parcel he hoped would make him look heroic. Then he went by the ordinary checked road.

canal_p13_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_066.text: Han paid his store crew for moving their private goods into the high dry room. The reserved hoist and four tagged planks remained intact for the cooper's later delivery, and the thirty-two deposit money stayed set aside. His ordinary store cash paid today's handling, distinct from that envelope. He wanted the private buyer's agent to know the goods had not been abandoned. The agent sent acknowledgment and kept the original security date. Preparation changed actual storage, not the contract's remaining forty-eight.

canal_p13_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_067.text: Tian stayed in her own room finishing the cover invoice and an unrelated small seam. The gate seedling stood away from the open window so rain would not chill its pot. Yue visited during her accepted rest, wanting to hear the permitted work song again. Tian sang two lines and stopped at the known gap. They ate a plum without filling it from a remembered market version. Yue felt the room's quiet make the coming flood more frightening, because she now knew exactly what ordinary things it might disturb.

canal_p13_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_068.text: The fresh quarry reading arrived after noon. Its water level had fallen a little under the restricted clearing, but ridge rain continued and runoff still entered faster during the heaviest hour. The officer kept the public road receiver notified and the nearby approach closed to unnecessary carts. Luo's local mark now touched caution. She began the next precautionary response: exposed lower work would end before the route's retreat limit, with the household's slower departure initiated while the ground remained dry enough for its actual pace.

canal_p13_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_069.text: The grandmother received the full departure instruction at the nearer corner, repeated by the named road worker. This was not rehearsal. She left the pot, took the prepared light sack already at hand and walked beside him toward the bench. The owner closed the ordinary shutter and joined them after checking nobody remained inside. The son was still on his booked parcel journey, with the actual message sent to his receiver. Yue did not make the woman wait for his return to give the departure a tidier family shape.

canal_p13_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_070.text: They reached the higher landing before water entered the checked inner strip. The grandmother rested at the bench and then completed the route within the allowance measured twice. The owner's nephew met them with a spare room his household had offered for two precautionary nights, bedding and ordinary meals from its existing pantry included. This finite family hospitality added no charge to the emergency allocation. The grandmother wanted her cup set on its own cloth. Yue helped unwrap it only after asking.

canal_p13_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_071.text: The gardener finished moving his remaining low baskets by the private cart's actual level route. Some unharvested beans stayed in the field. He wanted to know whether leaving them meant accepting any future loss. Luo said no; the ordinary crop account and later claims would preserve actual evidence without asking him to remain beside threatened rows. He took the family to higher lodging. The low field now had nobody standing in it to make damage harder for the canal to admit.

canal_p13_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_072.text: The nearer household-close board stayed in its checked ordinary position until the current crossing readings left the accepted condition. Bao ended work there rather than tightening it against an untested head. The control would not become a flood wall through his hands. The crew withdrew by the clear route, leaving the seasonal spill to its gravity path and observing from the higher marks. Yue walked with the field sheet under her cover. The larger water question had begun, and the answer would be found from dry ground whenever dry ground remained available.

canal_p13_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_073.text: Jiang received the current lower withdrawal and kept the powered apparatus within its own guarded accepted location. The small upper pocket's feeder remained isolated from planned test flow, with current head watched independently. If that local position left its rating, its crew would retreat too. Her new paid readiness hours continued at their actual time. Yue made an ordinary recovered-route check and put the tile away. A flood elsewhere did not authorize a command here until the prepared job itself had conditions it could meet.

canal_p13_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_074.text: On the thirty-second morning, upper rain darkened the ridge continuously. The local canal rose faster after dawn, and loose sticks began touching the ordinary caution mark. Luo ordered all cargo held at higher moorings and delivered the actual closure to both landing receivers. The keeper replacement helped her observe the ordinary gate from its protected position; neither climbed onto the moving leaf to improve a reading. Bao kept the lower strip closed. Most people now saw the danger the distant notes had described before their own sky changed.

canal_p13_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_075.text: The public drainage officer's next message reported part of the quarry stock bank slumping after the restricted outlet cleared. Water had begun passing the overflow lip in an uneven stronger run. He could describe its present direction toward the upper branch, not its future peak. The road receiver warned the canal through the timed runner route. Luo called the funded crew to its next actual response interval. The warning had arrived before the sharper local rise, but with less spare time than any morning meeting could have promised.

canal_p13_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_076.text: Yue carried the actual warning summary to the higher household shelter, where the grandmother's son had finally arrived from his parcel journey. He wanted to return for the heavy grain tub. His mother showed him the light sack and said the tub could wait for checked ground. The owner asked for the current house view through the appointed observer, not a private expedition into the hollow. Yue gave the actual next report time. Fear remained, but the people who had once argued at the doorway were already somewhere higher.

canal_p13_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_077.text: Before dark, Bao and the road crew checked the final inner return from their protected station. The outer clay dip carried a growing brown run, while the house yard stayed visible beyond it. The current observation post still met its footing limit. The gardener's dry bean boundary began disappearing under scattered shallow water. Bao called that actual change and moved the observers to the next higher mark. Yue heard the call from the accepted relay. The storm had finally reached ground drawn three times, and the drawing would now follow its changing feet.

canal_p13_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p13_078.text: Tian found Yue beneath the sheltered landing after the observers moved higher. She had delivered the paid covers and brought her own coat against the rain. 'Are you frightened?' she asked. Yue said yes, grateful that the answer could be so small. Tian said the grandmother had wanted to know whether the apprentice ate supper. They shared a rice parcel purchased with Yue's ordinary wages. Beyond the shelter, brown water crossed the old bean line. Yue kept eating until Luo called for the next real report.
